entries.text: Cisplatin has high nausea/vomiting risk. Agree prevention and rescue anti-sickness medicines, prescribed hydration and electrolyte replacement. A separate white-cell growth-factor plan may be chosen for clinical need. Do not add diuretics or change fluid intake yourself.

Cisplatin has high nausea/vomiting risk; doxorubicin and high-dose methotrexate have moderate risk. Each visit needs its own reconciled anti-sickness prescription. Methotrexate hydration, alkalinisation, level monitoring and folinic acid rescue must continue until the specialist team confirms safe clearance. Delayed clearance may need intensified rescue or glucarpidase. No fixed discharge day is promised. Low blood counts or a delay to the next chemotherapy dose must not automatically withhold or stop folinic acid rescue for methotrexate already given.

Mifamurtide has moderate nausea/vomiting risk. Agree an individual anti-sickness plan without automatically adding routine dexamethasone or chronic steroids, which may oppose immune-cell activation. Paracetamol or an antihistamine may be prescribed for infusion symptoms; adult examples are not paediatric doses. Preventive inhaler treatment may be considered for asthma or chronic obstructive lung disease.

This combination has high overall nausea/vomiting risk and requires white-cell growth-factor support for every cycle, timed by local prescription. Mesna reduces bladder injury but does not protect the kidneys or brain. Pharmacy must review anti-sickness interactions, particularly aprepitant, and specify all delayed and rescue treatment.

This high-dose regimen has high nausea/vomiting risk and requires white-cell growth-factor support. Mesna and prescribed hydration are essential but do not remove kidney or brain toxicity. The anti-sickness plan needs specific interaction review and coverage for treatment and delayed symptoms.
